bar: default@3565201 (`skills/desk-review/references/review-bar.md`) · tier MEDIUM · 3 files reviewed: `desk/bin/borrow.mjs`, `desk/bin/pass.mjs`, `tests/test_borrow.mjs`

**Seats.** The named agents are not registered in an autopilot worker (`--setting-sources ""`). So every Claude seat ran as `general-purpose`, told to follow its agent file:
- correctness: `lena-code-reviewer`
- tests and simplicity, one seat: `mira-playwright-expert`
- requirements: `bea-business-analyst`

Codex (cross-vendor) read the diff cold. Finders ran on their default model (no §3b finder model).

**Range.** The branch was rebased onto `main` (`e525bee`) after round 2, so round 2's commit `beb9c94` is no longer an ancestor. The fix range is therefore the whole branch, `e525bee..3565201`. The rebase changed only an import context line in `pass.mjs`. `main`'s own commits were not reviewed.

### Findings
None. Codex: NO FINDINGS. Correctness: NO FINDINGS. Tests and simplicity: NO FINDINGS.
- It confirmed the round-1 P0 is fixed: the cap-1 and cap-3 cases each give the slot to exactly one batch, and `tests/test_borrow.mjs:442-448` tests this.
- It confirmed the round-1 P2 is fixed: `pass.mjs` passes `otherBatches` filtered to the repo, and no second reader is left.
- `repoBudget` has one consumer, `desk/bin/pass.mjs:962`, which is the same module boundary `machineBudget` uses.

### Requirement gaps
- **AC2**, "Given two batches running passes at the same moment, when they count free slots, then no slot is handed to both."
  - This holds only while `takeBorrowLock` is held, from `desk/bin/pass.mjs:947` until it is released after the spawns are recorded.
  - The lock fails when another pass has held it over 120s, or when it cannot be made (`desk/bin/borrow.mjs:289-292`). Then `repoBudget` counts unlocked, as `machineBudget` already does, and `pass.mjs:968` only adds `(counted without the lock: …)` to the line.
  - Closing it needs a decision: start nothing when there are sibling batches and no lock, or accept the fallback.

### Scope
No out-of-scope hunks. `otherBatches` now takes `live` from `liveBeat`, which also changes how borrowing decides liveness. AC3 and AC4 need that, so that a waiting named batch keeps its slot.

### Earlier rounds
- **Round 1 at `fcc552e`:**
  - P0 `desk/bin/borrow.mjs:174`: the standing batch with nothing running and a named batch each kept the last slot for the other. Fixed.
  - P2 `desk/bin/borrow.mjs:132`: `repoBatches` restated `otherBatches`. Fixed.
  - Both were confirmed cross-vendor and fixed in `beb9c94`, now `3565201`.
  - Rejected: a P0 that a failed borrow lock lets the repo count run unlocked. This is the documented fallback `machineBudget` shares; it is tracked as the AC2 gap above.
- **Round 2 at `beb9c94`:** no findings, 1 gap (the same).

bar: default@13a1849 (`skills/desk-review/references/review-bar.md`) · tier LOW (no HIGH or MEDIUM production path, 196 lines) · 3 files reviewed: `desk/bin/borrow.mjs`, `desk/bin/pass.mjs`, `tests/test_borrow.mjs`

**Seats.** correctness `lena-code-reviewer` · tests `mira-playwright-expert` (added: a test path changed) · simplicity (`general-purpose`, desk-kiss Phases 2–5) · requirements `bea-business-analyst` · codex read the diff cold. Every seat ran.

**Range.** The verdict line names the fix range `3565201..13a1849` (one commit). Every finder, codex included, was asked to read the whole PR diff, `origin/main...13a1849`, and to give the fix commit particular attention. Bea read the whole branch, as she always does.

**Run note.** The first codex cold read got a brief that a parallel review had overwritten. It read PR #272, so it was discarded. Codex was re-run on a brief kept private to this review and read #271 at `13a1849`: NO FINDINGS. The Claude seats saw the same mix-up and reviewed #271 directly. Their bar text is the same file at this head, so they used the right bar.

### P0 (1)

**`desk/bin/pass.mjs:968`: the no-lock hold from 13a1849 is not recorded as a hold, and it fires when no sibling batch is live.** Confirmed by codex.
- **The hold is not recorded.** `heldWhy` (`pass.mjs:2102-2107`) has no branch for `repoUnlocked`. `REPO.room` is still positive here, so the pass records `held: null` (`pass.mjs:2116`). desk-q's no-progress note only fires when `rec.held` is truthy (`desk-q.mjs:451`), so it never appears for this hold. The only trace is the `repo workers:` line.
- **It fires on the wrong condition.** `SIBLINGS` (`pass.mjs:943`) is true whenever another batch's `queue.json` exists on disk (`batches.mjs:22-26`). That includes an idle or finished named batch. Yet `repoBudget` counts that repo as unshared (`borrow.mjs:144-145`, room Infinity), so in that case there is no race to prevent.
- **The cost.** A lock that "cannot be made" (`borrow.mjs:289`, any errno other than EEXIST) fails on every pass. When it does, a standing batch on a repo that has ever run a named batch starts nothing on every pass, and nothing reaches the person. Before this commit, and under AC6's intent, it fell back to the uncounted plan.
- **Suggested fix.** Fail closed only when a sibling is actually live, running or unreadable. That is the filter `repoBudget` already uses (`o.error || o.live || o.running > 0`, `borrow.mjs:144`), not "a queue file exists". Add a `repoUnlocked` branch to `heldWhy`, before the `REPO.room` check, with the `repoLine` text, so the hold is recorded and desk-q can raise it.

### Requirement gaps
None. Bea finds AC1–AC6 met at `13a1849`. AC2's round-3 gap is closed: with siblings, a pass can only spawn while it holds the lock (`pass.mjs:947`, `968-969`), and the lock is held until the spawns are recorded (`pass.mjs:1471`). Tests: `tests/test_borrow.mjs:356-372`.
- She notes one thing she did not count. `SIBLINGS` is read before the lock (`pass.mjs:943`), so a named batch created mid-pass could race a standing pass once. She could not show it happening, so it is not reported as a gap.

### Scope
No out-of-scope hunks.

### Other seats
- Tests: NO FINDINGS. The new no-lock test (`tests/test_borrow.mjs:365-372`) really makes the lock fail (ENOTDIR through `DESK_LOCK_DIR`), and it fails without the fix.
- Simplicity: NO FINDINGS.
- Codex cold: NO FINDINGS.

### Earlier rounds
- Round 1 at `fcc552e`: a P0 (last slot left empty) and a P2 (`repoBatches` restated `otherBatches`). Both fixed.
- Round 2 at `beb9c94`: none.
- Round 3 at `3565201`: one AC2 gap, now closed by `13a1849`. The P0 above is in that fix.

branch feat/DS-308-batches-share-worker-cap → main · round 5 · fix range only · 2 files · MEDIUM tier · correctness + tests + requirements + simplicity + codex cold
bar: default (`skills/desk-review/references/review-bar.md`)@1088c7a · agents: general-purpose fallback for correctness, tests and requirements (the named agents are not registered in this worker; each seat read its agent brief file) · finders on the session model

**No P0, P1 or P2 findings.** This round checked that the round-4 P0 is fixed. The worker was 31 commits behind main, so the branch was rebased onto `origin/main` before the push. There were no conflicts, and `git range-diff` shows all four commits patch-identical. Round 4's `13a1849` is now `f27113e`, and the fix range is the one commit on top of it.

What the round-4 P0 asked, and what `1088c7a` does:
- **The hold fired on the wrong condition.** `repoUnlocked` (`desk/bin/pass.mjs:970`) now holds a pass only when the borrow lock could not be taken *and* a sibling batch is live, running or unreadable. That is `repoBudget`'s own filter (`desk/bin/borrow.mjs:144`), applied to the same `repoBatches` list (`pass.mjs:962`). An idle or finished sibling no longer stops a batch.
- **The hold was not recorded.** `heldWhy` gains a `repoUnlocked` branch before the `REPO.room` check (`pass.mjs:2109`), carrying the `repoLine` text. `pass.held` is set, so desk-q's no-progress note can raise it.
- **Tests** (`tests/test_borrow.mjs`):
  - A running sibling with no lock: nothing starts, and `pass.held` names the lock.
  - An idle sibling with no lock: the batch starts its 2 and prints no repo-workers line. This test fails against the old code.

Checked: the codex cold read, plus correctness and tests, ran at `1088c7a`, and all returned NO FINDINGS. Simplicity and requirements read the pre-rebase head `3321ed3`, which is patch-identical, and also returned NO FINDINGS. Requirements found all six DS-308 criteria met and nothing out of scope.

Tests at `1088c7a`: 1723 checks across 20 suites passed under the test lock: every suite that runs `pass.mjs`, plus borrow and desk-q.

Not a finding: the requirements seat noted that the PR description still describes the AC2 gap as open. This fix try changed no description.

**P0** The no-lock hold added here is not recorded as a hold, and it fires when no sibling batch is live.

- `heldWhy` (`pass.mjs:2102-2107`) has no `repoUnlocked` branch, so the pass records `held: null` (`:2116`) and desk-q's no-progress note (`desk-q.mjs:451`) never fires.
- `SIBLINGS` (`:943`) is true for any other batch's queue file, idle or finished included, while `repoBudget` treats that repo as unshared (`borrow.mjs:144-145`).
- So when the lock cannot be made (`borrow.mjs:289`), a standing batch starts nothing on every pass, and nothing reaches the person.

Fix: gate on a sibling that is live, running or unreadable (`borrow.mjs:144`'s filter), and give `heldWhy` a `repoUnlocked` branch before the `REPO.room` check. Confirmed by codex.
